note: Both sets cover the four-column lighting-levels table and the Title 24 switch/vacancy-sensor requirements, and both repeat every table fact twice (with and without its activity condition). Set A additionally captures the bulb-equivalence facts from the prose, getting the 7W LED equivalence right, while Set B omits both equivalences entirely. However, Set A misreads the CFL equivalence as 5W where the page says 9W, and Set B garbles the 'HIGH CONSTRACT' label as 'CONRAST' in one quote. On balance A captures more of the page's engineering content with one value error, while B drops two important facts.
remarks: Text layer omits the graphic's LIGHTING LEVELS table entirely; all table claims were verified against the page image. The graphic itself contains the typo 'HIGH CONSTRACT' (for CONTRAST), which Set A reproduces faithfully and Set B mangles further as 'CONRAST'. Both sets miss: the definition of efficacy (light output vs. electric input), the statement that the LED bulb has higher efficacy because it puts out more light per watt, that low-efficacy luminaires may be paired with vacancy sensors and dimmer switches, and that dimmer switches allow gradual adjustment of light output/energy consumption. Both sets also state each table fact twice (once bare, once with the activity condition), inflating the claim counts.
